steps.name: open_events_list
steps.purpose: Open the events list at /orders. Use this — not open_create — for any test about the list itself: its rows, filters, tabs, or the Create Event control.

steps.name: expect_events_list
steps.purpose: Assert the events list actually rendered: the Create Event control is present and no error is shown.

steps.name: expect_create_options
steps.purpose: Open the Create Event menu on the events list and assert which paths it offers. Use for any case about what a tenant is offered when creating an event (eRFX, single-stage, BOQ). Case-insensitive substring match per option.

args.options: array of option texts that MUST be present, e.g. ["eRFX","Single Stage"]
args.absent: array of option texts that must NOT be present (optional)

steps.name: expect_url_contains
steps.purpose: Assert the browser's current URL contains this text (a path, or a query parameter like projectCreation=true).

args.text: the substring the URL must contain

steps.name: filter_events
steps.purpose: On the events list, switch to a tab: Live, History, Drafts or Recurring.

steps.name: expect_event_in_list
steps.purpose: Search the events list by title and assert a matching row exists. Defaults to the title this plan gave its own event, so use it after publish or save_draft to prove the event is where the case says it should be.

args.title: title text to search for; omit to use this plan's own event title

steps.name: expect_event_status
steps.purpose: On the events list, find the event's row by title and assert its status label contains this text (e.g. Draft, Live, RFQ in Progress, Closed). Defaults to this plan's own event title.

args.status: status text the row must show
args.title: title to look for; omit to use this plan's own event

steps.name: expect_template_selected
steps.purpose: Assert the current stage has a template applied — the picker no longer offers 'Select Templates' — and, when a name is given, that the stage shows it.

args.name: substring of the expected template name (optional)

steps.name: expect_sheet_columns
steps.purpose: Assert the pricing sheet's header row has rendered from the template. With no args, asserts at least one column exists; with columns, asserts each named key is present (e.g. price, quantity, buyer_hub).

args.columns: array of header keys that must be present (optional)

steps.name: open_stage_menu
steps.purpose: Open a stage tab's ⋮ overflow menu (Edit title / Delete …) and leave it open, so expect_disabled / expect_enabled can check its items. Defaults to the first stage tab.

steps.name: expect_disabled
steps.purpose: Assert a named control on the current screen is DISABLED (greyed out / aria-disabled). Use for rules like 'Save as draft is disabled until…', 'Delete is disabled while one stage remains', 'Savings is disabled before a template'. Matches buttons, menu items and tabs by their visible text.

args.control: the control's visible text, e.g. "Save as draft", "Delete", "Savings"

steps.name: expect_enabled
steps.purpose: Assert a named control on the current screen is ENABLED and clickable. The counterpart of expect_disabled.

steps.name: place_counter_offer
steps.purpose: Buyer side, on Master QCS after a vendor has bid: open the vendor's Counter Offer from their column header, enter a counter price in the drawer's sheet, add a remark and send it. The product offers the control only while the bid is live and active. Use open_master_qcs first.

args.vendor: vendor name whose bid to counter (default: the first with a Counter Offer control)

steps.name: expect_counter_offer_sent
steps.purpose: Assert the comparison grid now marks the vendor's bid with a counter offer (the 'Counter offer initiated' mark).

steps.name: close_event
steps.purpose: On a PUBLISHED event's page, make the event CLOSED: Settings → "End <status>" (the product's force-end, where the tenant allows it) — otherwise wait for the bidding window to lapse. Pair it with set_schedule{minutes: 3} before publish so the wait is short. Use before cases that need a closed event (Master QCS on a closed event, awarding after bidding has ended).

args.maxWaitMinutes: when the tenant has no force-end, how long to wait for the bidding window to lapse (default 6)

steps.name: open_event
steps.purpose: Open an EXISTING event — by project id (direct) or by title (search the events list and click the row) — landing on its project page. Use it for cases about an event that already exists, or to return to the event this plan created (default: this plan's own title).

args.title: event title to search for (optional; defaults to this plan's own event)

steps.name: capture_screen
steps.purpose: Record evidence of the current screen — a screenshot and the accessibility tree — under a label, without asserting anything. Use when a case wants to inspect or document a screen, or when the next thing to test has no step yet and a person needs to see the controls that exist.

args.label: short name for the capture, e.g. "order-details-counter-offer"

steps.name: open_participants
steps.purpose: On a PUBLISHED event's project page, open the stage's Participants list (the surrogate-bid drawer lives here). Reaching the list is the success condition — it is paginated and only eligible vendors show an Add Bid control. Reports how many rows offer Add Bid.

steps.name: open_master_qcs
steps.purpose: On a published event with bids, open the Master QCS tab and assert the comparison grid rendered with its line items and bidding vendors. Optionally name vendors that must appear.

args.vendors: array of vendor names that must be in the grid (optional)

steps.name: configure_single_stage
steps.purpose: On the SINGLE-STAGE create screen (open_create path single-stage), open the configuration drawer and set the event type; for an auction, its strategy and the awarding rule. This is where auction strategy is chosen on this build — rank, price or traffic light; knockout and dutch exist only through RFQ→Auction conversion.

args.awarding: "lot" (entire lot to one vendor) | "line_item" (partially, multiple vendors)
args.rangeLower: traffic light only: lower bound of the specified range (optional)
args.rangeUpper: traffic light only: upper bound of the specified range (optional)

steps.name: convert_to_auction
steps.purpose: On a PUBLISHED RFQ's project page (after publish + expect_published), open Settings → Convert to Auction and continue. The app opens the converted event's create screen in a new tab, which becomes the page for every later step. Knockout and dutch auctions are reachable only this way.

steps.name: open_create
steps.purpose: Open the event-create screen. Always the first step of a create test.

steps.name: compose_stages
steps.purpose: Set the stages exactly. RFQ and Auction cannot coexist; at most two stages. Auction is the default stage, so asking for anything else is a real change.

steps.name: set_title
steps.purpose: Give the event a title.

args.title: string; omit to auto-generate a unique one

steps.name: switch_stage
steps.purpose: Move to a stage's tab. Required on a multi-stage event: template, sheet, questionnaires and evaluator all apply to the CURRENT tab only, so each stage must be configured on its own tab.

steps.name: select_template
steps.purpose: Pick the stage's pricing template. Required before line items can be added.

args.name: substring of the template name; omit to take the first offered

steps.name: add_line_items
steps.purpose: Add line items through the Manage Line Items drawer.

args.search: optional product search text to use for all of them

steps.name: fill_sheet
steps.purpose: Fill the pricing sheet for every line item on screen.

steps.name: fill_questionnaires
steps.purpose: Technical stages only: give every RFI section (the global Vendor Assessment and one per line item) a template and fill blank questions.

steps.name: assign_evaluator
steps.purpose: Technical stages only: assign an evaluator to every control that needs one.

steps.name: set_schedule
steps.purpose: Open the schedule drawer and commit it. Needed before publish.

steps.name: invite_vendor
steps.purpose: Put vendors on the event. Name them when the test cares WHICH vendor bids — a bid test must be able to sign in as that company — otherwise the product's own audience is used.

args.count: minimum number of participants required; fails if the audience cannot supply it

steps.name: publish
steps.purpose: Publish the event and wait for the outcome.

steps.name: save_draft
steps.purpose: Save as draft instead of publishing.

steps.name: expect_line_items
steps.purpose: Assert the toolbar badge shows this many line items.

steps.name: expect_published
steps.purpose: Assert the browser reached a real project page with an id.

steps.name: expect_no_error
steps.purpose: Assert the application showed no error message.

steps.name: expect_error
steps.purpose: Assert the application DID refuse, optionally matching its wording. Use for negative tests.

args.contains: optional substring the message must contain

steps.name: place_bid
steps.purpose: Sign into the VENDOR PORTAL as a vendor and submit a quote for the event just published. This is the vendor bidding for themselves. Needs the vendor to have been invited.

args.vendor: vendor name; defaults to the configured vendor account

steps.name: place_surrogate_bid
steps.purpose: Enter a bid FOR a vendor from the buyer console, without leaving it (surrogate bidding). Use when the test says the buyer bids on a vendor's behalf. Not available for knockout or dutch auctions, nor for technical stages.

args.vendor: vendor name; defaults to the first vendor offering Add Bid

steps.name: award_event
steps.purpose: Award the event after bidding: Master QCS -> Start Awarding -> allocate line items -> Create Proposal -> submit. Needs a published event that has at least one bid.

args.vendor: vendor to award to; defaults to whichever bid can be allocated

steps.name: expect_awarded
steps.purpose: Assert the award went through (a proposal was created and submitted).

steps.name: expect_bid_submitted
steps.purpose: Assert the vendor's bid was accepted (the vendor portal shows the stage as Submitted).

steps.name: expect_publish_blocked
steps.purpose: Assert the event CANNOT be published yet: press Publish and confirm either the confirm button is disabled or the app refuses. Use for tests about a precondition not being met.

args.because: optional substring of the message you expect

steps.name: expect_stages
steps.purpose: Assert exactly these stage tabs are present.
